name: Granularity-Driven Cut
definition: A voxel selection strategy that keeps the full octree in host memory and places only a selection of voxels on the GPU based on their projected size, ensuring fine voxels near the camera and coarser voxels farther away, bounded by a maximum resident voxel count $n_{\text{max}}$.
summary: Granularity-Driven Cut selects octree voxels based on projected size constraints to optimize GPU memory usage, distinguishing itself by using geometric limits rather than importance scores.
